name: The Tomb
notes: rows: one string per row, north row first. One character = one cell. All rows the same length.
cell: width of a cell in metres. Heights are in metres.
floor, ceil = floor and ceiling height.
slope + rise = the floor climbs by 'rise' toward that side (N, E, S or W). 'floor' is the low end.
steps = draw that slope as this many stairs.
water = height of the water surface in that cell.
torches: cell [column, row], the wall it hangs on, height above that cell's floor.
items: things lying in the level: id from data/items.json and the cell. 'at' [east, south] 0..1 places it within the cell. 'inside': ids of things in it, if it is a bag.
Keep things very few, and give each a reason to be where it is: beside the remains of whoever carried it, among grave goods, in a den.
props 'remains': what is left of someone (kind bones) or of a jackal (kind jackal). It cannot be picked up. Put belongings beside it as items.
carry: ids of things the player starts with. The first goes in the left hand, the second in the right, the rest on the belt.
creatures: id from data/creatures.json and the cell it starts in. 'at' places it within the cell, as for items.
spots: places that say something when you stand there. 'wall' puts a door picture on that wall. 'to' is the level it leads to.
auto:true = no door: you go to that level as soon as you enter the cell (a flooded passage). 'face' is the way you look when you arrive there.
props: scenery that stands in the level. id 'urn' = a big clay urn; kind: whole, broken or tipped; size = height in metres; 'at' as for items.
gates + buttons: a gate with mode 'button' is drawn as plain wall. A button (cell, wall, h, opens) works the gate with that id once: rumbling and water, then the gate slides back for good.
start: cell [column, row] and the way the player faces.

spots.text: A burial, broken open long ago. The bones were thrown about.
A dead jackal. The others have been at it.
Someone died here, a long time after the tomb was shut.
